results.summary_before: Potato-1 is the control logic for a Brainfuck CPU, decoding the eight Brainfuck instructions plus HALT and NOP into register increment/decrement and memory read/write control signals. It reads instruction, zero flag and IO wait inputs on each rising clock edge and updates its output pins on the falling edge, pausing on Put/Get until IO wait is released. Using it requires external hardware: three bidirectional counters for program counter, data pointer and value, a ROM for instructions, a RAM for data, and TTL gates for write control. The design is deliberately minimal and slow, and the documentation notes it is only the control portion of a CPU rather than a complete processor.

results.summary_before: This design implements a 4-trit balanced ternary program counter with up, down, and hold counting modes, as well as jump/load capability. It also includes a 3-trit asynchronous balanced ternary radix converter that converts to signed binary and back. The design is written in MRCS and tests the capabilities of the MRCS Verilog generator and Tiny Tapeout's bidirectional pins. It is verified on an FPGA with a provided testbench, and the ASIC version is functionally similar.

results.summary_before: This circuit drives a 16x16 P10 LED panel, initially displaying the string 'TT03P5'. It accepts a 1.2 Mbaud UART input to paint pixels, erase pixels, clear the display, and change the displayed color, but resource limitations restrict it to a single color at a time and no double buffering. A mode pin allows selection between two clocking patterns to accommodate different panel wiring. External hardware includes an LED panel and a level converter to 5V logic.

results.summary_before: The design implements an SPI peripheral with an 8-byte RAM, 324-byte ROM, and a random source, supporting standard and quad SPI read/write commands. It is intended to be used as a ROM for an RP2040, allowing it to boot from the ROM, and also provides debug access via switches and a 7-segment display. Silicon testing showed that the SPI RAM works and the RP2040 boots from the ROM, but writes to the RAM were not functioning and the random source distribution is non-uniform. The project requires a custom RP2040 board and a PIO-based SPI master for full testing.

results.summary_before: This is a fully combinational 4-bit ALU containing a ripple-carry adder, a carry-lookahead adder, a matrix multiplier, a Wallace-tree multiplier, a comparator and a barrel-shifter, selected by a 3-bit opcode on the bidirectional pins. The two 4-bit operands come from the input pins, and the 8-bit result appears on the outputs, with the barrel-shifter using b[1:0] for shift width and b[2] for direction. No clock is required, and a silicon test report confirms the adder was verified on the bringup stream. It is a compact educational ALU demonstrating several arithmetic architectures in one tile.
